materials.title: The first pancake
materials.text:

Soon a line formed. I began cooking faster, but Leo stopped taking new orders for a moment. We already had six waiting, and only two pans. I thought he was losing us ____5____. He pointed to a family who had asked twice when their food would be ready.

We needed to tell people the ____6____ before they ordered. Leo wrote "About ten minutes" on a card. Some people left, but those who stayed knew what to ____7____.

By closing time, the table was sticky and my arms were ____10____. We counted the money only after washing the pans and putting everything ____11____. Our teacher asked what we had learned.

"To cook smaller pancakes," I said at first. Then I added that serving food meant making promises we could ____12____. Leo had not been slowing the stall down for no reason. He had been keeping our plans ____13____.

The broken first pancake went into our food-waste box. Its lesson stayed with me: a busy stall needs more than ____14____. Next time, I would watch both the pans and the people ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.

materials.title: A bus made of cardboard
materials.text:
For our science display, Nia and I built a model bus from cardboard. We wanted visitors to see how its wheels moved. Our first plan was to make the outside look exactly like a real ____1____. We painted tiny windows.

When we tested it, one wheel would not ____2____. A thick piece of cardboard was pressing against it. We could fix the problem only by cutting a hole in our beautiful side panel.

"We'll spoil it," I said. Nia asked what the model was meant to ____3____: the paint or the moving parts. I knew the answer.

We cut the hole carefully. Now we could reach the wheel and remove the extra cardboard. The opening looked ____4____. Then Nia suggested covering it with a clear sheet rather than more paint. Visitors would be able to look ____5____.

On display day, we set a sign beside the model: "Push gently." A hard push sent the bus towards the ____6____ of the table. I caught it just in time. We moved it to the centre and added two low blocks to stop it travelling too ____7____.

Visitors asked about the opening. Some wanted to know why one wheel had stuck. We showed them the piece we had ____8____. It became a useful part of our explanation.

I had expected a good model to hide every ____9____. Instead, showing our repair helped visitors understand the mechanism. Our teacher praised us for making the movement ____10____ to see.

Beside our original design, we recorded what we had ____11____. The bus was less like a perfect toy but better as a ____12____ tool. Before our next project, we agreed to test the important parts ____13____ we decorated them. A mistake could cost less time if we found it ____14____. And a small window into our work could make the whole idea ____15____.

questions.explanation: The project is explicitly a model bus. The other objects are not its intended appearance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A wheel pressed by cardboard cannot turn. Shining, sleeping and opening are not the needed wheel movement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A science display should show the moving parts. Cost, hide and eat do not express the display’s teaching purpose.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The cut opening is unattractive until covered. Finished, silent and round do not state the appearance problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.

materials.title: The walk without torches
materials.text:
On a guided evening walk, we left our torches switched ____1____ for a few minutes. We stood still on the familiar path while our eyes adjusted.

At first, I heard almost ____2____. Then a bicycle bell sounded beyond the trees. A bird moved in the leaves. Water ran under a little bridge. In daylight, I usually passed these places too ____3____ to notice.

On cards, we drew maps of the ____4____ we heard, not identify every animal. Amir heard a soft clicking. I thought it came from the bridge; he thought it was behind us. We marked our different ____5____ with two arrows.

Later, we found a loose sign moving in the wind. Neither arrow had pointed exactly at it. I wanted to rub mine out. Amir suggested keeping both and adding the real ____6____. Our map could show what we had learned.

Near the gate, a loud phone rang. Its owner silenced it and stepped away to answer. We were not trying to make the park completely ____7____. We were learning which sounds we usually missed.

We compared cards. No two maps were the ____8____. Different people had stood in different places, and some sounds had lasted only a moment. The guide asked us to explain the ____9____ before deciding anyone was wrong.

I had brought a camera but taken no photographs. Yet I had a detailed ____10____ of the evening: our arrows, notes and questions. I realised that paying attention did not always mean looking more ____11____. Sometimes it meant giving another sense a chance.

Next weekend, I listened from that bridge in daylight. The water was still there, but traffic partly ____12____ it. I added the time to my notes. A sound map, I discovered, was a record of one ____13____, not a permanent description. Leaving room for changes made it more ____14____. I now carried a pencil as well as a torch, ready to ____15____ what I noticed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Torches are switched off briefly while standing safely. The other particles do not express extinguishing their light.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The subsequent discovery of quiet sounds contrasts with initially noticing almost nothing. Music is absent; everything reverses the progression; traffic is not the initial statement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Hurrying past prevents noticing quiet sounds. Carefully would encourage notice; silence and lateness do not explain the missed detail.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: This is explicitly a listening map. Colours, people and buildings are not the assigned features.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
